intro: Ravi Menon looks after the Windows servers at Delmar Manufacturing, a company with a head office, a factory and four branch sites. He knows his way around Active Directory, but now head office wants everything managed from Azure too, without moving anything out of the building. Ravi picks AZ-802 to keep up.
Follow Ravi through a year of hybrid server work, with his cluster, file servers and domain controllers.

active-directory-domain-services: Delmar has just merged with a smaller firm and now has two forests. Ravi sets up a trust so users in either can sign in to the other, then tidies up who holds which special roles and how replication moves changes around. He learns how Group Policy settings stack up, how to recover an accidentally deleted account, and how to give services their own self-managing accounts.
hybrid-management-clustering-virtualizat: Head office wants alerts and policies applied to the branch Hyper-V hosts. Ravi connects them to Azure for management without moving any workload, and uses a web-based tool for daily tasks. He learns how to patch a failover cluster without downtime, how a cluster keeps its quorum with a witness in the cloud, and how virtual machines can move between hosts.
on-premises-hybrid-networking: With a central site and several branches, Ravi redesigns DNS and DHCP. DNS zones that live in the directory replicate on their own and securely. DHCP pairs split or back up each other so that no branch loses its addresses. He also looks at how DNS can be signed to prove its answers are genuine, and at the choices for linking sites to Azure.
storage-file-services: Users at three file servers are about to get a single path to their files, with the contents kept in sync between sites. Ravi learns how to join local disks into pools with resilience built in, why mirrored and parity layouts are different trade-offs, and how to reclaim space by removing duplicate data. He also compares file systems for the job they are given.
securing-windows-server: After a security review, Ravi hardens the file servers and the most sensitive administrator accounts. Only approved programs may run, even for a local administrator; credentials in memory are protected; local administrator passwords are rotated automatically; and powerful accounts are limited in how they can sign in. A tool that watches the directory for signs of attack completes the picture.
monitoring-troubleshooting-windows-serve: Ravi’s last project is to make the hybrid fleet look the same, whether a server is in Azure or on the factory floor. Every server captures the same counters, sends them through the same agent, and alerts on the same rules. He also ties patch status into a single view. For the first time, a problem on any server gets the same kind of report.

epilogue: On the day of the exam Ravi remembers the factory floor, the old file server in the corner, and the new view that shows every server in one place. Hybrid no longer sounds like a buzzword. He settles in and starts reading the first scenario.

active-directory-domain-services: Ravi blocks inheritance on an OU to stop a company-wide Group Policy from reaching it. The policy arrives anyway, because it was marked Enforced, and enforcement beats blocking. A department finds its desktop wallpaper has become the company logo. The department is furious. Ravi mutters something about the order of precedence and closes the door.
hybrid-management-clustering-virtualizat: Ravi sets up Hyper-V Replica and tells the branch manager, ‘If the host dies, you won’t notice.’ The host dies, and the manager notices very much, because the replica needs to be failed over and it does not run on its own. Live migration is a different tool, for a different day.
on-premises-hybrid-networking: Ravi creates a stub zone and tells everyone the DNS records are ‘replicated’. A stub zone only knows where to find the authoritative servers, not the records themselves. The branch can resolve nothing for an hour. The DNS servers, to their credit, kept saying ‘ask them’.
storage-file-services: Ravi turns on data deduplication on the volume holding the live database ‘to save space’. The savings are tiny and the database is unhappy. Deduplication loves file shares and backup libraries; a constantly changing database is the one thing it cannot stand. Ravi puts it back the way it was.
securing-windows-server: Ravi turns on credential protection on a server and an old application that depends on a legacy sign-in suddenly stops working. The old application’s developer left in 2013. Ravi learns that every security feature has a cost, and that someone should have checked the legacy applications first.
monitoring-troubleshooting-windows-serve: Ravi sets a log-query alert for a fast CPU spike, ‘because it is more powerful’. It checks every five minutes with a delay and misses the spike entirely. A simple metric alert would have caught it in seconds. Not every nail needs the most sophisticated hammer.

active-directory-domain-services.problem: Two forests, many policies and special roles, and no clear control or recovery plan.
active-directory-domain-services.cause: Directory structure, trust, replication and policy inheritance interact in ways that surprise people.
active-directory-domain-services.solution: Trusts, FSMO roles, Group Policy precedence, recovery tools and managed accounts bring order.
active-directory-domain-services.next: Next, managing servers across on-premises and Azure.

hybrid-management-clustering-virtualizat.problem: Servers are managed in two different worlds and patched without coordination.
hybrid-management-clustering-virtualizat.cause: On-premises hosts are invisible to Azure and clusters are updated by hand.
hybrid-management-clustering-virtualizat.solution: Arc, Windows Admin Center, cluster-aware updating, witnesses, live migration and replication unify and protect.
hybrid-management-clustering-virtualizat.next: Next, the networking that ties sites together.

on-premises-hybrid-networking.problem: Sites cannot reliably find or address each other.
on-premises-hybrid-networking.cause: DNS and DHCP are configured per site, and failover is manual.
on-premises-hybrid-networking.solution: Zone types, DNSSEC, DHCP failover and VPN or private link choices make name, address and link services resilient.

storage-file-services.problem: Users cannot find files, and storage is wasted or unprotected.
storage-file-services.cause: Files are scattered across servers and disks are used inefficiently.
storage-file-services.solution: DFS, Storage Spaces, Deduplication and the right file system unify, protect and shrink the storage.

securing-windows-server.problem: Servers and admin accounts are attractive targets.
securing-windows-server.cause: Attackers who get a foothold can run anything and steal credentials.
securing-windows-server.solution: Application control, credential protection, LAPS, Protected Users and identity monitoring limit and detect abuse.
securing-windows-server.next: Next, monitoring and troubleshooting the fleet.

monitoring-troubleshooting-windows-serve.problem: Problems appear on some servers and nobody sees them all.
monitoring-troubleshooting-windows-serve.cause: Monitoring differs on each server, and patch status is unknown.
monitoring-troubleshooting-windows-serve.solution: Counters, event logs, Azure Monitor, alerts and Update Manager give one consistent view.
monitoring-troubleshooting-windows-serve.next: That completes the lessons. Next come the cheat sheet, the word bank and the practice questions.
